introduction: “We must look upon every human being we saw as a letter from the Beloved to us. No matter how blotted, blurred, torn or soiled that letter appears to be.” The guide moves from that way of seeing, through the “sin-covering eye” that will not speak of another’s faults, to forbearance in teaching, pardon of personal injuries, patience under persecution and the return of good for evil; and it marks one boundary, that the community punishes what the person forgives. The companions show how widely this is taught. The Sermon on the Mount, Paul’s “overcome evil with good”, Peter’s “charity shall cover the multitude of sins”, the Qur’an’s “repel the evil deed with one which is better”, the Dhammapada’s “hatred ceases by love” and Lao Tzu’s “recompense injury with kindness” all stand with the readings; Esau, Joseph, David and Stephen are its stories. The objections are also old. Confucius asked what is left to give kindness if injury is repaid with kindness; Leviticus and Proverbs command rebuke; Blake warns of wrath unspoken; Shylock speaks for the wronged; and Claudius asks whether pardon is possible while the offence is kept.
questions: “See in every human being only that which is worthy of praise.” Is this a discipline of perception, a rule of speech, or both? What would it be like to practise for a week?
Leviticus says to rebuke a neighbour “and not suffer sin upon him”; the readings say to be silent about faults and to help correct them “through kindness”. How would you put the two together?
Confucius: “With what then will you recompense kindness?” What answer do the readings, or Paul, or Lao Tzu, give him?
Reading 12 forbids personal revenge and keeps communal punishment. Take an actual case, a theft or a slander. What does the wronged person owe, and what does the community owe?
Peter asked for a number. Reading 75 tells of a man forgiven four times. Is there a point at which forgiveness should stop, and does reading 10 name it?
“May one be pardon’d and retain the offence?” What part does the offender’s repentance play in these readings?

outside.why: Every human being a letter from the Beloved, however blotted or torn. Whitman: I find letters from God dropt in the street, and every one is sign’d by God’s name.
The ground of the image: God created man in his own image.
See in every human being only what is worthy of praise. Whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report, think on these things.
Look toward people themselves and you will be unhappy. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; thinketh no evil; beareth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

Compassion for all, except those with a selfish motive or disease of the soul: kindness cannot be shown the tyrant or the thief. Be ye wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. Where does this guide draw the limit of forbearance?

Retaliation by the injured person is revenge and blameworthy. Ye have heard, An eye for an eye: but I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

The reading keeps punishment for the community while forbidding revenge to the person. Paul makes the same division: the ruler beareth not the sword in vain. Is the line between pardon and public protection easy to hold?
Let your adorning be forgiveness and mercy. Portia: the quality of mercy is not strain’d; it is twice blest; it blesseth him that gives and him that takes.
Search out your own imperfections and not another’s. Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
Dwell on your own development and close your eyes to others’ deficiencies. Be kindly affectioned one to another; in honour preferring one another.
Well is it with the righteous one who does not revile the sinful. He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone.
Cover a friend’s shortcoming with the hem of concealment. Have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.
The proverb behind Peter’s sentence: hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.
“This is called error, not hatred; forgetfulness, not rebellion.” Pope’s line: to err is human; to forgive, divine.
Be silent about others’ faults, pray for them, help them correct them. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.

Leviticus forbids the grudge and commands the rebuke in the same breath: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. The readings prefer silence. When is silence about a fault the loving course, and when is it Leviticus’s “suffering sin upon him”?
Know that you are less than anyone else. In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
See one another’s good qualities and cover misdeeds. The Qur’an: neither backbite one another; would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother?
Mention nothing but good of people. Speak evil of no man; be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
Proverbs speaks for the other duty: open rebuke is better than secret love; faithful are the wounds of a friend. Can a community that praises everyone still tell the truth to its members?
Look not upon the shortcomings of one another. Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
One word is like fire, another like light. A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Do not view the sayings of others with too critical an eye. Ben Sira: admonish a friend, it may be he hath not said it; for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.
If someone cannot yet grasp a truth, show forbearance. Paul on the weaker conscience: it is good not to do any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth.
Impart the Word according to the hearer’s measure. I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for hitherto ye were not able to bear it.
Guide the peoples with the utmost patience and forbearance. Marcus Aurelius: men exist for the sake of one another. Teach them then, or bear with them.
Do not dispute with one who hesitates. The servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves.
With those who deny religion, be tolerant and patient. The servants of the Beneficent, when the foolish address them, answer: Peace.
Overlook shortcomings, that differences be dispelled. Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any.
Overlook one another’s faults for My name’s sake. Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
It is not befitting to take one another to court. Paul to Corinth: why do ye not rather take wrong? why do ye not rather suffer yourselves to be defrauded?
See only others’ good actions. Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
Joy at hearing that the friends overlook small mistakes and forgive enemies. Blessed are the peacemakers.
Forgive him from the heart; we all look to God’s pardon. The parable’s master: I forgave thee all that debt; shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant?
The same condition stands in the prayer Christians say daily: and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
Excuse him and forgive his past shortcomings; he will make up for them. If he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times turn again, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
Four times he repented and was accepted again. Peter asked whether seven times was enough: I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
Forgiveness sought at once on another’s behalf. When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The reading quotes this verse: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins.
To pardon is an attribute of the Lord. The Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin.
At an unreasonable word, look to the root of the tree and not its leaves. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.
Be kind to the violators at first; do not be severe. Count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
The time of separation will come; for now forbearance, lest division occur. Let both grow together until the harvest.

Borne in patience and silence, until the other began to embitter the weak. Blake’s poem warns about silence of another kind: I was angry with my foe: I told it not, my wrath did grow. What distinguishes the patience of the reading from the nursed wrath of the poem?
Beware lest any of you seek vengeance, even on one thirsting for your blood. Avenge not yourselves: vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
Keep faith with the one who is cruel to you. Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not.
Respond to malevolence with a friendly heart. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he between whom and thee there was enmity will become as a bosom friend.
Meet condemnation with love and kindness; do not argue. Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you, bless them that curse you.
Praise those who speak ill of you. Being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it; being defamed, we intreat.
Requite evil with good and censure with praise. Lao Tzu: recompense injury with kindness.

Confucius was asked about that very saying and demurred: with what then will you recompense kindness? Recompense injury with justice, and kindness with kindness. Is there an answer to his question in the readings?
Count the enemy as a friend. To those who are good to me, I am good; and to those who are not good to me, I am also good.
The way of the people of Bahá is to return evil with good. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
Confront them only with kindness. The Dhammapada: hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.

Hurt no heart, even an oppressor’s. Shylock gives the logic of the other course from inside: if you wrong us, shall we not revenge? The villainy you teach me I will execute. He has been wronged, and the play does not let the audience forget it. What do the readings ask of someone in his place?
Regard the sinner as sinless. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
He came at last in shame and fell at His feet. Jacob expected a wronged brother’s revenge: and Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
“I did not embarrass him.” Hath no man condemned thee? Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
Whatever one sees from others, one must overlook. The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
Those who plotted now seek reconciliation; “we have no quarrel with anyone”. I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves.
A man who acted treasonably is received as a trusted friend. David to Saul, who was hunting him: the Lord had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: but mine eye spared thee.
He laughed: the man only reveals his own state; be kind to such. Bacon: in taking revenge, a man is but even with his enemy; but in passing it over, he is superior.
An eye for an eye converted into love your enemies. Leave there thy gift before the altar; first be reconciled to thy brother.
He would have kissed the hand of his would-be murderer. Stephen, under the stones: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
Be forbearing one with another. With longsuffering, forbearing one another in love.
The attributes of beasts of prey befit not man. Prospero, with his enemies in his power: the rarer action is in virtue than in vengeance.
The attributes of the people of faith. The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness.
View the weak and inconstant with the eye of perfection. The Lord is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish.
Patience is called for, and trust in God. Jacob in the Qur’an, deceived by his sons: comely patience! And Allah it is Whose help is to be sought.
Consider what the followers of Christ endured. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord.
“Give glad tidings to the patient ones.” They on the good ground bring forth fruit with patience.
If anyone revile you, be patient and trust in Him Who hears. Wait on the Lord: be of good courage.
Days will come when you will ask pardon for those cruel ones. Joseph, years after: ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
Overlook the faults of others. The verse reading 212 expounds: those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good.
If someone transgresses against another, the wronged one should forgive. When ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any.

“And pardon men.” Of a woman known as a sinner: her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little. Does being forgiven make a person forgiving?

“Verily God forgiveth all sins.” Claudius, trying to pray, finds a limit on his own side: may one be pardon’d and retain the offence? What do the readings ask of the one forgiven? Reading 75 mentions repentance four times over.
Cover the errors of these destitute ones. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

shortfall: The readings of stretches six, eight and nine are short exhortations to patience and kindness in nearly the same words, and several are personal letters about a single offender; companions were placed where a reading says something distinct, and the rest were left with their neighbours’.

matthew-unmerciful-servant.text: Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee

genesis-esau-ran-to-meet-him.text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept

genesis-be-not-grieved.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt. Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life

mark-when-ye-stand-praying.text: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses

luke-seven-times-in-a-day.text: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him
